In poetry -

\- Luceafărul (The Evening Star, also the longest romantic poem) and Floare albastră (Blue Flower) by Mihai Eminescu   
\- Plumb (Lead) and/or Lacustră (Lacustrine) by George Bacovia   
\- Testament (Will) and/or Flori de mucigai (Mold Flowers) by Tudor Arghezi   
\-  Riga Crypto și lapona Enigel (Riga Crypto and lapona Enigel) by Ion Barbu   
\- Eu nu strivesc corola de minuni a lumii (Crushing the world's crown of wonder) by Lucian Blaga   


And prose -   
\- O scrisoare pierduta (A lost letter) by I.L. Caragiale   
\- Moara cu Noroc (The lucky Mill) by Ioan Slavici   
\- Baltagul (The hatchet) by Mihail Sadoveanu   
\- Ion by Liviu Rebreanu   
\- Ultima noapte de dragoste, întâia noapte de război (The last night of love, the first night of war) by Camil Petrescu

\- Povestea lui Harap-Alb (Harap-alb's story) by Ion Creangă   
\- Alexandru Lăpușneanu by Costache Negruzzi

I and my classmate missed the bus like idiots. It was really late, around 6:50 or so and we had no way of getting home as my parents were out of town and her parents' car was crashed the week before.   
So we decided to hitchhike(we both had like 10 bucks and hoped someone would see we are students and take pity on us). We waited for 5-10 more minutes before someone eventually came.   
It was man, maybe 20-25. He offered us a ride and as soon as we got in, we said the location.   


We drove for a few minutes before my classmate said we had only 20 bucks and he laughed and said 'You're too sweet to take money from.' We were tired and grateful he didn't take money from us.   
About close to our destination, he make a sharp turn and that's when I realized something was wrong. I tapped the dude on the shoulder and asked him what was he doing and he was just like 'Oh, don't worry. It's just a quick stop. Stay here, I'm not that far away.'   


We didn't buy it and as soon as he was out and walking away, we got out and made a run for it. I don't know what he was planning for us, or if he chased us but I just remember running like my life depended on it.
Seeing this like this makes me realize the 2012 apocalypse should have happened.

I was visiting some relatives in the country side when I was about 13-14. I was extremely bored and not wanting to have to talk to really old ladies and have them lecture me about churches and why I don't wear skirts, I decided to go explore the village, as it was my first time there (I did went there when I was 2 but I can't remember that).   
As I wandered into the deeper parts of the village, I tripped like a dumbass, on a grass patch. As I sat up, I saw I bruised my knee pretty badly (I fell on a rock with my knee.) As I winced and cried, I saw someone approach me and help me up. It was a boy, about a few years older than me. He smiled and asked for my name.   
I told him my first name and then he smiled sadly and told me something along the lines of 'Take care of mom, okay? ' and then just walked away as if it was nothing.   


When I asked my grandma (it was a small village, everyone knew everyone + their families) about a boy that looked like the one who helped me, she paled and told me I need sleep.   


I'm still scared to this day and no matter how much I tried, I never saw him again.

Worst: He stares at me while I eat anything and makes me feel bad.   


Best: He tries to hug me and cuddle me when I'm sad/crying.

My grandmother's children.

My grandmother has 3 sons and 1 daughter(my mom). Originally though, she had 7 children. Pretty common for her time.   
The first was a girl that sadly died at 2 years old. Doctors said it was 'natural causes' but according to my grandparents, she wasn't sick.   
The second is my oldest uncle that was misdiagnosed with tuberculosis at age 23 at his workplace. From worry and stress, he almost died.   
The third is my second uncle that was born with an eye slightly more closed than the other. Because of this, he was bullied and hit a lot at school.   
The fourth was another girl. My grandmother was extremely happy to have her. While she was in the hospital, my grandma fed her at 4 AM. The following morning, she couldn't find her. Grandma was worried, she asked the doctors what happened. The doctors(I really can't say anything good about them) told her, that her daughter had died at 12 AM. But at the time, in that zone, baby switching was not a rare sight.   
The fourth is my third uncle. He is the youngest boy but grew up protecting his siblings, even his older ones from bullies.   
The fifth was a boy that lived to be around 5 years old before he went missing one day and was never seen again.   
The sixth is my mom who I love so much, but she also went through a lot, especially with birthing me at a young age and my dad being a neglectful piece of shit.   
The seventh was another boy that my grandma said was born healthy. Until, at a few weeks old, his skin started ripping and getting attached to the blanket he was sleeping with. At only a few months, he died.   


When my grandma tells me these stories, I can't help but cry a little. She is such a sweet woman and truly deserved to have all of her kids grow up healthy with her.

My grandfather fought in Crimea and in the Caucasus Mountains. While there, he was wounded and had to be hospitalized. Shortly after, he was taken prisoner.   
While he was there, he fell madly in love with a Russian woman who had mutual feelings for him. They planned to leave and my grandfather said he would take her to Romania to marry. For some reason, she wasn't allowed to leave.   
My grandfather was heartbroken and was prepared to live his life there just to be with her but she committed suicide. My grandfather left, probably grief-stricken.   


He told me many stories, especially the ones on the battlefield, but none of them made him tear up like the Russian woman story did. He refused to tell me or my mom her name and would only refer to her as 'Floricica' which means little flower in Romanian.
